explanations.explanation: You nailed it, baker! Ruth 1:1 says when the famine hit Bethlehem in Judah, the family went to reside in the land of Moab. Packing up everything and moving to another country is a huge deal. They headed right across the border to find food.

Egypt is famous for folks running to it during famines, but not this family! Ruth 1:1 tells us this man took his wife and two sons to reside in the land of Moab. They crossed over eastward instead of heading down south.
Not Edom this time, friend! Ruth 1:1 says the family left Bethlehem in Judah to go reside in the land of Moab. That is where Elimelech and his family settled down to escape the famine.
Spot on, baker! Ruth 1:4 says the two sons took Moabite wives, one named Orpah and the other named Ruth. Her name is right on the front of the book! That little family is growing out there in Moab.
Rachel is way back in Genesis, baker! In Ruth 1:4, the two Moabite women who married Naomi's sons are named Orpah and Ruth. Ruth is the one who joins this family tree.
Dinah is Jacob's daughter from way back in Genesis. Ruth 1:4 tells us Naomi's sons married two women from Moab named Orpah and Ruth. Ruth is the daughter-in-law we are following!

That is the sad truth, baker. Ruth 1:5 tells us both Mahlon and Chilion died after living in Moab about ten years. First her husband, and now both of her boys. Naomi is left completely on her own without her sons or her husband.

explanations.answer: Her house in Moab burns down
explanations.explanation: No house fire in this story, friend. The heartbreak in Ruth 1:5 is that both of her sons, Mahlon and Chilion, died. Naomi was left without her husband and without her two boys.

explanations.answer: She falls sick and loses her sight
explanations.explanation: The text does not mention Naomi losing her sight, baker. Ruth 1:5 tells us the tragedy is that both of her sons, Mahlon and Chilion, passed away. That left her all alone in a foreign land with her two daughters-in-law.

You got it, baker! Ruth 1:6 says Naomi heard in Moab that the LORD had attended to His people by providing them with food. The famine back home was finally over! That good news is what got her packing her bags.

Israel does not have a king yet in these days, baker. Ruth 1:6 says Naomi heard the LORD had visited His people by providing them with food. Bread was back on the tables in Bethlehem, which means House of Bread!

Not a military victory this time, friend. Ruth 1:6 tells us Naomi heard that the LORD had attended to His people by providing them with food. After all those years of famine, Bethlehem finally had bread again.

explanations.answer: Go back to their mothers' homes
explanations.explanation: That is it, baker! Ruth 1:8 says Naomi told her two daughters-in-law, 'Go back, each of you to your mother's home.' She loved them enough to tell them to return where they had family and a future.

explanations.answer: Walk faster to beat the dark
explanations.explanation: She was not trying to set a walking pace, friend! Ruth 1:8 tells us Naomi stopped them on the road and said, 'Go back, each of you to your mother's home.' She wanted them to return to their own families in Moab.

explanations.answer: Stay close to her the whole way
explanations.explanation: Naomi was actually trying to do the exact opposite, baker! Ruth 1:8 shows she told both Orpah and Ruth to go back, each of them to her mother's home. She did not want them dragging along into an uncertain future in Judah.

You got it, baker! In Ruth 1:9, Naomi says, 'May the LORD enable each of you to find rest in the home of your new husband.' She genuinely wanted them to be blessed with new homes and peace back in Moab.

It is actually true, friend! Ruth 1:9 shows Naomi praying for both young women: 'May the LORD enable each of you to find rest in the home of your new husband.' She wanted them to remarry and have security.

explanations.answer: We will return with you to your people
explanations.explanation: Right on the money, baker! Ruth 1:10 says both women wept and told her, 'Surely we will return with you to your people.' They loved Naomi so much they were ready to leave their homeland behind with her.

explanations.answer: We will stay in Moab and wait for you
explanations.explanation: They were not planning on waiting behind, friend! Ruth 1:10 tells us both daughters-in-law wept aloud and said, 'Surely we will return with you to your people.' At first, both of them refused to leave her side.

explanations.answer: We will come visit you in Bethlehem
explanations.explanation: This was way more than a visit, baker! In Ruth 1:10, they wept and said, 'Surely we will return with you to your people.' They were ready to move all the way to Judah right alongside her.

explanations.answer: Would you wait for them to grow up
explanations.explanation: Spot on, baker! In Ruth 1:13, Naomi asks them if they would really wait around for baby sons to grow into grown men just to marry them. She is laying out the cold hard math to show them they need to go home!

explanations.answer: Would you raise them as your own
explanations.explanation: Naomi was talking about future husbands, not adoption, friend! Ruth 1:13 shows her asking if they would wait for newborn sons to grow up and refrain from getting married in the meantime. She knew that made no sense for them.

explanations.answer: Would you go ahead to Bethlehem
explanations.explanation: She was trying to send them back to Moab, not ahead to Bethlehem, baker. In Ruth 1:13, Naomi asks, 'would you wait for them to grow up? Would you refrain from having husbands?' She was showing them how impractical staying with her was.

explanations.answer: The LORD's hand has turned against her
explanations.explanation: You found the reason, baker. Ruth 1:13 tells us Naomi says, 'it is much more bitter for me than for you, because the hand of the LORD has gone out against me.' She felt like God Himself was opposing her after losing everything.

explanations.answer: The people of Judah have turned against her
explanations.explanation: She had not even made it back to Judah yet, friend! Ruth 1:13 shows Naomi saying it is bitter for her because 'the hand of the LORD has gone out against me.' Her grief ran very deep.

explanations.answer: The people of Moab have turned against her
explanations.explanation: The text does not say the Moabites turned on her, baker. In Ruth 1:13, Naomi explains her deep bitterness by saying, 'the hand of the LORD has gone out against me.' She felt God's hand heavy on her life.
That is true, baker! Ruth 1:14 says the women wept aloud again, and Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye. She took Naomi's advice and turned back to head home to Moab.
It really is true, friend! Ruth 1:14 tells us they wept aloud, and Orpah gave Naomi a goodbye kiss. After hearing Naomi's reasons, Orpah decided to return to her mother's home.
Actually, Ruth stayed right where she was, baker! Ruth 1:14 tells us that while Orpah kissed her goodbye, Ruth clung to Naomi. Ruth was not going anywhere without her mother-in-law!
You got it, baker! It is false because Ruth refused to leave. Ruth 1:14 says Orpah kissed Naomi goodbye, but Ruth clung to her. She stuck by Naomi like fresh dough to a counter!

Spot on, baker! In Ruth 1:15, Naomi points at Orpah walking away and tells Ruth, 'Look, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and her gods; follow her back home.' Naomi gives her one last chance to turn around.

It is definitely true, friend! Ruth 1:15 says Naomi told her, 'Look, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and her gods; follow her back home.' Naomi really tried to convince Ruth to follow Orpah.

explanations.answer: Naomi's God will be her God
explanations.explanation: That is the big moment, baker! In Ruth 1:16, Ruth makes that famous declaration: 'your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.' She is not just choosing Naomi; she is choosing the LORD!

explanations.answer: She will take care of Naomi's house
explanations.explanation: Ruth goes way deeper than chores, friend! Ruth 1:16 tells us she promised, 'your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.' That is a total commitment of heart and faith.

explanations.answer: She will learn all the ways of Judah
explanations.explanation: Ruth's vow was much bigger than learning local customs, baker. In Ruth 1:16, Ruth tells Naomi, 'your people will be my people, and your God will be my God.' She joined herself fully to Naomi and the God of Israel.
You got it, baker! In Ruth 1:17, Ruth says, 'May the LORD punish me, and ever so severely, if anything but death separates you and me.' That is total lifelong loyalty right there!
Distance was not going to stop Ruth, friend! Ruth 1:17 shows her calling down a severe punishment if anything but death separates them. She was in this all the way to the end of life.

Ruth was not letting new marriage prospects pull them apart, baker. Ruth 1:17 tells us she vowed that only death would ever separate her from Naomi. She put her whole life on the line with that promise.

explanations.answer: She stops trying to persuade her
explanations.explanation: That is right, baker! Ruth 1:18 tells us when Naomi saw that Ruth was determined to go with her, she stopped trying to persuade her. There was no changing Ruth's mind after a speech like that!

explanations.answer: She sends her back after Orpah
explanations.explanation: Naomi did not keep pushing, friend. Ruth 1:18 says once Naomi saw how determined Ruth was, she stopped trying to persuade her. She accepted that Ruth was walking that road with her.

explanations.answer: She tells her to wait in Moab
explanations.explanation: They were already on the road out of Moab, baker! Ruth 1:18 tells us that when Naomi saw Ruth's fierce determination, she stopped arguing. They turned together and kept walking toward Bethlehem.

You nailed it, baker! Ruth 1:19 says when they arrived, the whole town was stirred and the women exclaimed, 'Can this be Naomi?' Ten years of grief and hardship had changed her so much they could barely believe their eyes.

They did not ask about Elimelech right away, friend. Ruth 1:19 says the women of the town looked at her in shock and asked, 'Can this be Naomi?' She looked completely different after all those hard years.
They recognized Naomi, but she looked worn down, baker! Ruth 1:19 tells us the women of Bethlehem exclaimed, 'Can this be Naomi?' The whole town was buzzing seeing her walk back in.

That is it, baker! In Ruth 1:20, Naomi tells them, 'Do not call me Naomi... Call me Mara, because the Almighty has dealt quite bitterly with me.' The name Mara means bitter, and she felt every bit of it.
Hannah is Samuel's mother over in 1 Samuel, baker. In Ruth 1:20, Naomi tells the women to call her Mara instead. She wanted a name that matched the bitterness she was carrying in her heart.
Leah is Jacob's wife back in Genesis, friend. Ruth 1:20 tells us Naomi said, 'Do not call me Naomi... Call me Mara.' She chose Mara because it means bitter.
She actually said the exact opposite, baker! In Ruth 1:21, Naomi says, 'I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty.' She left with a husband and two sons, and came back with neither.
You got it, baker! It is false because Naomi said, 'I went away full, but the LORD has brought me back empty' in Ruth 1:21. She felt completely drained of everything she once had.

Perfect bake, friend! Ruth 1:22 tells us Naomi and Ruth arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest. The fields are full of grain, and that timing is going to matter a whole lot in this story!
Wheat harvest comes a little later in the season, baker! Ruth 1:22 specifically tells us they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest. The grain is just starting to be brought in.
No olive harvest on this card, friend. Ruth 1:22 says they arrived in Bethlehem at the beginning of the barley harvest. Just as food returns to the land, these two widows arrive in town.
